title: Runtime target belongs in the package name, never in the scope
subject: main
summary: The tier scope expresses reuse scope only. Runtime target is a separate axis and enters the package name: `@libs/web-components`, `@libs/web-layouts`, `@libs/mo

adr.context: The UI libraries are nested a level deeper than every other library — `shared/libs/ui/web/*` and `shared/libs/ui/mobile/*` — but a package identifier is flat. Two packages were both really "components", so the mobile one carried its platform in its name and the web one did not. That asymmetry was a name collision being worked around, not a decision.
adr.decision: The tier scope expresses reuse scope only. Runtime target is a separate axis and enters the package name: `@libs/web-components`, `@libs/web-layouts`, `@libs/mobile-components`.
consequences: One scope per tier survives; no `@libs-ui-web/*` sub-scopes.
Every UI library states its platform — none by accident, none by omission.
Folder nesting stays as it is. A package identifier does not inherit folder depth, so any distinction the tree makes must be restated in the name or it is lost.
